ai.description: Ravi’s Bush Frog is a small rhacophorid (20–23 mm) with a brown dorsum and distinct dark interorbital markings. It features a pale cream venter and granular skin texture on the back.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes ravii* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid reddish-orange iris, which contrasts sharply with the dark, mottled brown coloration of its body.
ai.habitat: Ravi’s Bush Frog inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Ravi’s Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively foraging for small insects among the foliage of its high-altitude forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes ravii* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. Breeding occurs during the monsoon, with females laying small clutches of eggs in vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: Ravi’s Bush Frog is endemic to the high-altitude shola forests and grasslands of the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, India.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes ravii* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude shola forests.
